title: Cock-a-Leekie
subtitle: Scottish chicken and leek soup with prunes
excerpt: Scotland's national soup: chicken pieces simmered slowly with leeks until the broth is rich and silky, finished with prunes that add a faint sweetness to the savoury base. A deeply restorative bowl.

recipe.sourceNotes: Cock-a-leekie is one of the oldest documented Scottish dishes, appearing in records from at least the sixteenth century when it featured at a state banquet for James VI. The name describes the dish simply: a cock (an old cockerel) cooked with leeks. The inclusion of prunes, while seemingly strange, is traditional and documented in the earliest Scottish recipes: they contribute a gentle sweetness that balances the savoury richness of the long-simmered chicken broth. The dish was originally made with a whole old cockerel, which required the long simmering to become tender; modern cooks use a whole chicken or chicken pieces, which need less time. The soup is considered Scotland's answer to pot-au-feu and was served at the dinner to mark the opening of the new Scottish Parliament in 1999.

recipeTools.notes: A very large saucepan or stockpot.

content.text: Skim the broth regularly in the first 20 minutes: a grey foam rises as the chicken proteins coagulate, and removing it produces a cleaner, clearer soup. Add the prunes towards the end of cooking so they plump but do not dissolve entirely. The soup is traditionally served with the chicken shredded back into the broth, not in whole pieces.

items.preparation: jointed into 4 to 6 pieces, or use bone-in thighs and drumsticks
cleaned and sliced into 2 cm rounds; use white and light green parts

content.text: Place the chicken pieces in a large pot with the onion, carrot, thyme, bay leaves, and 1.5 litres of cold water. Bring slowly to a simmer over medium heat, skimming off the grey foam as it rises. Season with salt. Simmer gently, uncovered, for 45 minutes.

Remove the chicken and the carrot and onion. Add the sliced leeks to the broth and simmer for 20 minutes. Pull the chicken meat off the bones and shred it, discarding the skin and bones. Return the chicken to the pot.
Add the prunes and simmer for a further 10 minutes until plumped and tender. Remove the thyme sprigs and bay leaves. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Serve in deep bowls scattered with parsley.
